reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: front face with purple stripes and a dark inset with a brown post

answer.evidence: Rows 0-2 are a full-width cream band (16 px wide) that ends in a brown front-edge line at row 3. Row 4 is a darker brown eave shadow, which matches evidence (a). Below it, rows 5-15 are a vertical front face made of dark and purple-blue stripes, with a small brown post at rows 7-10 near x=8. The top band is only 3 rows tall, which is thin, but it has both an edge line and eave shadow. The brown strip on the right edge is a frame outline, not a receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny signboard on a purple base, not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. The measured facts are fine: 10 visible tones, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% near-neutral dark edges, so the outline is tinted rather than black. But the whole piece uses only 10 colours in total, against 185 and 66 for the references. By eye the board, its edge and the base each get about 2-3 tones. There are no tile scallops, no plaster or stone grain, and no clustered texture. It looks thinner and flatter than either reference, and sparseness alone is not the reason; the missing material ramps and grain are. Next to the references it reads as a simple sticker-like prop. Because it is the wrong kind and clearly shallower in shading, I fail it.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny signboard-like prop: a white/cream board with a brown edge on a purple post. It is not a whole building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. It is about the size of a single tile, with no roof tile scallops, plaster speckle or stone shading. Its 10 distinct colours across the whole piece compare with 185 and 66 for the references. The 10 visible tones per tile and 0% near-flat coverage are measured on a very small area and do not show comparable richness. By eye it has about 3 shading steps per material against 5-6 in the references. It has no roof, walls, door or windows, so it does not match the building references. The per-tile facts are not meaningful for a piece this small. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is not a whole building. It is a tiny sign-like prop (a cream board on a brown cap with a purple pedestal), about one tile across. It has no roof tiles, walls, door or windows, so it cannot be compared with the two full house references. Its measured facts (10 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat, 0% neutral dark edges) look fine, but they come from a very small area and say little about structure. By eye, its ramps are shallow, with about 3 steps per material against the references' 5-6 on tile roofs, timber and stone. It has no per-tile roof highlights, plaster speckle or stone-by-stone shading. Next to the references it looks thin and sticker-like. Its edge tint is only mildly material-toned, so I call it mixed. The kind mismatch alone fails it: a building cell holds a sign prop.
